cases.purpose: Force EIO on the owned controlling terminal while retaining it for mode checks. Use guarded exact-child lifecycle controls and PTRACE_O_EXITKILL.
cases.oracle: A separate guarded Python termios probe must observe the same injected EIO and restore its original modes; the parent observer records real tty read arguments and the substituted kernel return.
cases.comparison: The PTY driver pauses at each intercepted /dev/tty read, observes ECHO/ICANON clear, releases it, then compares complete termios modes and exact unchanged private shadow bytes. Retain pre-cleanup failure, pidfd, wait/signal, descriptor and cleanup observations.
cases.setup_script:
[[ $EUID == 2000 && $PWD == /tmp/parity-case && $HOME == /tmp/parity-home ]] || exit 125
IFS= read -r v </sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor || exit 125
IFS= read -r u </etc/bashos-parity-vm || exit 125
[[ $v == QEMU && $u =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$ ]] || exit 125
/bin/cp /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/trace-vm-tty-fault-r2.py ./trace-vm-tty-fault-r2.py
/bin/chmod 0755 ./trace-vm-tty-fault-r2.py
/bin/cp /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/trace-vm-supervisor-r2.py ./trace-vm-supervisor-r2.py
/bin/chmod 0755 ./trace-vm-supervisor-r2.py
./trace-vm-supervisor-r2.py --selftest
/bin/chmod 0600 db/shadow
./trace-vm-tty-fault-r2.py --control
cases.candidate_script:
[[ $EUID == 2000 && $PWD == /tmp/parity-case && $HOME == /tmp/parity-home ]] || exit 125
IFS= read -r v </sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor || exit 125
IFS= read -r u </etc/bashos-parity-vm || exit 125
[[ $v == QEMU && $u =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$ ]] || exit 125
./trace-vm-tty-fault-r2.py candidate "$BASH" eio
rc=$?
[[ $rc == 0 ]] || exit 21
IFS= read -r ignored </dev/tty || exit 22
exit 0
